title: Two delivery routes
hook: The route of exposure changes the word.

knows: Animals have structures and behaviors that can be investigated.
doesNotKnow: The first arrow depicts a toxin delivered into another animal by a bite. Venom is delivered by an animal; poison is harmful when taken in or contacted by another route. The diagrams classify delivery, not a substance’s danger.

misconception: The evidence in the scenario supports a different interpretation.
objective: An animal delivers a toxin through a bite. Which term describes that delivery?

claims.text: The route of exposure changes the word. An animal delivers a toxin through a bite. Which term describes that delivery? The first arrow depicts a toxin delivered into another animal by a bite. Venom is delivered by an animal; poison is harmful when taken in or contacted by another route. The diagrams classify delivery, not a substance’s danger.
claims.source: Unverified starting points, not a verified citation for this claim: OpenStax Biology 2e https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e ; Smithsonian National Zoo https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals . Exact claim-specific source and species qualifications require independent review.

claims.text: The two generic icons illustrate delivery routes, not specific species, doses or safety advice.
A toxin harms an animal after it eats the organism containing it. Which term describes this route? A substance that harms when eaten is described as a poison; venom is delivered by the animal.
